checks.q: What are the two elements of a head flow meter?
o: A restriction and a differential pressure measuring device
checks.x: The primary element is the restriction, and the secondary element is the differential pressure measuring device.

checks.q: What does a head flow meter actually measure?
checks.x: The head flow meter actually measures volume flow rate rather than mass flow rate.

body.text: The orifice plate is the simplest and most economical flowpath restriction. Plates are 1/16 to 1/4 inch thick, mounted between flanges in a straight run of smooth pipe.

body.alt: Three orifice plates: concentric with a center hole, eccentric with an offset hole, and segmental with a partial opening.

body.text: As fluid passes through the orifice, velocity rises to a maximum and pressure falls to a minimum.

checks.q: What are the two distinct disadvantages of orifice plates?
o: High permanent pressure drop and erosion
checks.x: Orifice plates cause a high permanent pressure drop and are subject to erosion.

checks.q: Which orifice plate is the most common?
checks.x: The concentric orifice plate is the most common of the three types.

body.alt: Venturi tube with a converging inlet, a cylindrical throat, and a diverging recovery cone.

body.text: Low pressure is measured in the throat, and high pressure upstream of the entrance cone.

body.alt: Dall flow tube with an inlet shoulder, a converging cone, a slotted throat, and a diverging exit cone.

body.text: The dall flow tube has a higher ratio of pressure developed to pressure lost than the venturi. It is more compact and is commonly used in large flow applications.

checks.q: Which is the most accurate flow-sensing element when properly calibrated?
checks.x: The venturi tube is the most accurate flow-sensing element when properly calibrated.

checks.q: About what is the pressure loss of a dall flow tube?
checks.x: This type of flow tube has a pressure loss of about 5%.

body.text: In its simplest form, a pitot tube is a tube with an opening at the end, facing the flowing fluid.

body.alt: Rotameter: a float in a conical glass tube that widens with height, with a calibrated scale.

body.text: With no flow, the float rests at the bottom. As flow increases, pressure drop increases, and the float rises to indicate the amount of flow.

body.alt: Nutating disk meter: a circular disk on a central ball inside a chamber.

body.text: The disk is attached to a central ball, with a shaft held in an inclined position by a cam or roller.
The volume needed for one revolution is known, so total flow is the number of rotations times that volume.

checks.q: What happens to the float in a rotameter as flow rises?
checks.x: The higher the flow rate the greater the pressure drop, and the farther up the tube the float rises.

checks.q: How does a nutating disk meter find total flow?
o: Disk rotations times a known volume per rotation
checks.x: Total flow is calculated by multiplying the number of disk rotations by the known volume of fluid.

checks.q: A D/P flow instrument has a leak on the high pressure connection. How does indicated flow compare with actual?
checks.x: A high-pressure leak lowers the differential pressure sensed, so indicated flow is less than actual.

checks.q: A D/P flow instrument has a leak on the low pressure connection. How does indicated flow compare with actual?
checks.x: A low-pressure leak raises the differential pressure sensed, so indicated flow is more than actual.

checks.q: What indication results from vapor in the liquid passing through a head flow meter?
checks.x: Pressure fluctuations from the vapor cause very erratic indication from the detector.

facts.q: How is flow related to differential pressure in a head flow meter?
facts.a: Flow rate is proportional to the square root of the differential pressure.

facts.q: What are the three kinds of orifice plates?
What are the major disadvantages of a venturi tube?
facts.a: High initial costs for installation and difficulty in installation and inspection.

facts.q: What does an extractor do in a flow detection circuit?
facts.a: It electronically calculates the square root of the differential pressure, giving an output proportional to system flow.

facts.q: How is pump differential pressure related to pump flow?
facts.a: It is proportional to the square of pump flow.

summary.text: Head flow meters place a restriction in the line to cause a pressure drop, and the differential pressure is converted to a flow measurement.
A rotameter uses a float in a conical tube, and a nutating disk wobbles as fluid passes through.
Changes in temperature and pressure greatly affect indicated steam flow.
The density of the fluid, ambient temperature, and humidity can affect flow sensing instrumentation.
